policy_engine.What is a policy engine in an agent syst: It decides whether each agent action is allowed, denied or modified, based on composable rules.
policy_engine.How do allow, deny and transform decisio: Any deny wins; transforms modify the action in order; allow only if no policy denies.
policy_engine.How do you order policies and resolve co: Evaluate in a fixed order, record every decision, and let deny override allow.
policy_engine.How do transforms chain?: Each transform receives the output of the previous one, in a deterministic order.
policy_engine.What happens when a policy raises?: Treat an exception as a deny (fail closed) and log it.
policy_engine.Fail open versus fail closed?: Fail open keeps things running when the policy system breaks. Fail closed is safer for dangerous actions.
policy_engine.Rule-based policies versus model-based c: Rules are predictable and auditable but brittle. Classifiers generalize but are probabilistic and can be attacked.

approval_gate.What is a human approval gate in an agen: A human must approve risky actions (payments, deletions, external messages) before they run.
approval_gate.What does the TTL protect against?: An approval given long ago should not authorize the action now, since the context may have changed or the approval was stale or stolen.
approval_gate.How do you classify an action as allowed: Map the action type and parameters to a risk tier with explicit rules, and default to needing approval or deny.
approval_gate.How do you bind an approval to the exact: Hash or key the approval on the exact action (tool plus canonical arguments) and check the match at execution time.
approval_gate.How do you handle an expired approval?: Treat it as missing: deny or ask again. Never run.
approval_gate.How do you balance safety against approv: Tier by risk, batch similar requests, and use scoped time-limited grants. Too many prompts get approved without reading.
approval_gate.What should be logged for audit?: Who approved what exact action, when, with what context, and the outcome.

guarded_runtime.What layers does a guarded agent runtime: Policy checks, human approval, redaction of secrets or PII, provenance tracking and audit logging.
guarded_runtime.Why does provenance of input matter?: Instructions from untrusted sources (web pages, tool output) should not get the same authority as the user. This is prompt-injection defense.
guarded_runtime.In what order do policy, approval, redac: Usually provenance and policy first, then approval, then execution, then redaction of outputs, with audit throughout. Say why each order matters.
guarded_runtime.How do you prevent untrusted content fro: Tag data with its source and refuse privileged actions whose trigger comes from untrusted content.
guarded_runtime.What does the audit record contain?: The action, arguments (redacted), provenance, decisions from each layer, the approver and the outcome.
guarded_runtime.Defense in depth versus a single policy: Several layers catch what one misses, at the cost of complexity and latency.
guarded_runtime.How do you test a guardrail stack offlin: Replay recorded traces and adversarial scenarios with fixed tool responses, and assert the decisions.
